input_facts_with_evidence.statement: FTCT causal structure: directed graph G=(V,E). The vertices are a subset of V_all={A..Z,a..z}, and each value q(v) ∈ VALS(v) ⊂ Z. Each edge carries op(e), which is addition or subtraction only, with q(v2)=op(e)∘q(v1). T(G) is the set of chains, and the depth N is the length of the longest chain.

input_facts_with_evidence.statement: Training data: child chains of length M<N are merged in order with M' noise vertices from V_all−V. The first child-chain value is uniform on VALS(u1), and later values follow the edge operations. Noise vertices get random values, and m=M+M'. Testing data: noise-free longest chains of length N. Complete test chains are not seen in training.

input_facts_with_evidence.statement: Few-shot format: doc^k := [seq^(1), \n, ..., \n, seq^(k)]; inp^k := doc^k + [v1, q1^(k+1)]; lab^k := [v2, q2^(k+1), ..., vL, qL^(k+1)]; k runs from 0 to K. Downstream processing turns these into natural-language-like sentences (inp~^k, lab~^k), and dec(lab~) := lab = [v2,q2,...,vN,qN].

input_facts_with_evidence.statement: Transformer implementation: Hugging Face GPT-2 architecture with 720-dimensional embeddings, a 2048-token context and GPT2Tokenizer index mapping, trained with AdamW at learning rate 5e-5. Appendix G.1 gives no training steps, batch size or seeds.

input_facts_with_evidence.statement: MLP implementation: sliding-window inputs of 150, 200 or 300 tokens, keeping the best-performing size (per-row size not reported). Inputs concatenate 503-dimensional one-hot token encodings, about 1e5 input dimensions at window 300. Hidden size 1000, varying layer numbers, output dimension 50257 with near-zero weights for unused tokens, AdamW at learning rate 5e-5. The windowing is motivated by the authors' statement that a 1-shot CoT prompt suffices for optimal model performance.
